text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- DIRECT INVESTMENT UP 51 PCT IN FIRST QUARTER

Foreign direct investment into Brazil in the first quarter of the year amounted to $1.769 billion, 51.3 percent over the same period of 1996. This figure does not consider the $929 million investment for the purchase of Banco Bamerindus by HSBC Holdings Plc.
-- TELEBRAS RISES ON RATE HIKE

Stocks of Telebras and its subsidiaries rose on Thursday on rumors of a telephone rate increase. The Communications Ministry late in the day announced new tariffs for the telecommunications sector, reducing existing cross subsidies between the different services.
-- VBC TO INVEST $24 BLN BY 2002
VBC Energia, a holding controlled by Grupo Votorantim, Camargo Correa and Bradesco, will invest up to $24 billion in the next five years.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- TWELVE MORE POLICE OFFICERS TO BE ARRESTED
The Military Police issued orders for the arrest of 12 more police officers due to their suspected connection with videotaped crimes committed by Sao Paulo police.
-- TORTURE BILL TO BE SENT TO CARDOSO
The Brazilian Senate approved on Thursday a bill that classified torture as a crime. The bill now must be signed into law by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
-- LOCAL TELEPHONE CALLS TO RISE 61 PCT
The government announced changes in Brazil's telephone rates. Local calls will rise 61 percent Friday, while residential subscription tariffs will rise 270.3 percent to 10 reais from 2.70 reais.
O GLOBO
-- SENATORS TO REMOVE BANK SECRECY PROTECTION OF SOME FUNDS
A congressional inquiry into a multi-million bond scam is likely to break the bank secrecy of pension funds allegedly involved in the scandal.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
